description.narrative: The proposed project will improve the Khevi-Ubisa section and improve operations and maintenance of the road network, as well as road safety. Further, the project's focus on climate resilient design will contribute to mainstreaming the sustainability of Georgia's road network.

description.narrative: Efficiency and safety of road transport along the EWH improved

Road crash rate per 100 million vehicle-km traveled on the EWH reduced by 30 percent of the existing national road crash rate (2017 baseline: 13.6) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Assessment of outcome shall be made at completion of works. Data Source: Roads Department's crash data statistics (annually)

Average travel time from Chumateleti to Argveta reduced to 45 minutes (2017 baseline: 71 minutes) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Assessment of outcome shall be made at completion of works. Data Source: Supervision consultant's annual project progress report
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 12 km section of EWH between Khevi and Ubisa constructed Indicator: By 2023: 12 km of new access controlled dual carriageway or 4-lane divided highway reconstructed and/or constructed to 80 km per hour design standard, partly on a new alignment (2017 baseline: 0 km) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Civil works contract for Khevi-Ubisa F2 road was signed on 20 Nov 2018 (Hunan Road and Bridge Construction Group Co. Ltd., PRC).
Contract for construction supervision consultant was signed on 30 Apr 2019 (UBM, Turkey). The consultant mobilized in May 2019.
ADB provided conditional no objection on Compliance Report 2 (CR2) on 22 Jul 2019 to enable RD to issue notice to commence to contractor. The Contractor officially mobilized on 22 Jul 2019.
Construction of main camp have been completed. Works are ongoing for the tunnels and bridges, as well as earthworks, slope protection, and temporary access roads.
To catch up with planned progress and eliminate lag in work performance, the Contractor and Engineer agreed to work two shifts and overtime. Amendment 6 to construction supervision consultant's contract was approved by ADB on 25 Mar 2020.
In spite of the COVID-19 pandemic, the F2 works have not been stopped and site works are underway even during the past 10 days (from 17 to 27 Apr) when movement of any vehicle had been stopped. Special permits were given by the government in order to continue the works.
In order to further ramp up the pace of the works, the Contractor is working partially in 3 shifts.
As of 11 Oct 2021, LARP implementation is more than 99.02% complete with only 1 land plot under expropriation.
LARP implementation completed at the end of December 2021 and Compliance Report 6 was approved in Feb 2022.
On 12 July 2022, ADB provided no objection to Addendum to CR1.
Expected completion of first 9 kms by Dec 2022, and complete project by May 2023.
On 22 Jul 2022, ADB provided no objection to the extension of F2 works until 31 May 2023 (Amendment 2).
Additional land acquisition of 8191 sqm. was identified during the construction stage. These cases were not reported through a LARP Addendum, however, the additional impacts are validated and reported in the compliance report No.7 prepared by EMC and submitted to ADB for review.
As of 30 Apr 2023, estimated progress of executed works for the Khevi-Ubisa Section (F2) is about 95.33%. 9 out of 12 kms is open to traffic, and works are ongoing on the remaining 3 kms.
Construction of the Khevi-Ubisa Section (F2) was completed, and the road was inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 28 Oct 2023. The works are under Defects Notification Period (DNP) until October 2025.
Since Contractor missed the sectional completion dates as agreed, the RD considers itself entitled to delay damages. However, these have not yet been deducted.
Construction of the Khevi-Ubisa Section (F2) was substantially completed, and the road was inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 28 Oct 2023. The works are under Defects Notification Period (DNP) until Oct 2025.
The winding up period is extended until 31 Dec 2025 to cater for the decision of the dispute board.
RD submitted the draft Borrower's PCR on 25 Jun 2025.
During the Oct 2025 pre-PCR mission, RD is requested to provide additional documents after completion of the traffic survey by 31 Jan 2026.
The PCR mission will be fielded in late Q1 2026. Board circulation is in Q2 2026. Data Source: Supervision consultant's project progress reports (annually)

Output: 12 km section of EWH between Khevi and Ubisa constructed Indicator: with at least three gender-inclusive features (2017 baseline: 0 km) Data Source: Supervision consultant's project progress reports (annually) Actual value:

Output: Road safety awareness increased Indicator: By 2023: Road safety awareness campaign messages reach at least 70% of the targeted total population (2017 baseline: not applicable) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: RD will complete internal consultations (with Patrolling Police, Ministry of Health, and other stakeholders) and provide a roll-out plan of the activities by Q3 2021; and based on it, RD will thereafter prepare terms of references (TOR) for the recruitment of the firms.
The project team and Roads Department agreed during MTR that the activities for the road safety awareness component, and capacity building for operation and maintenance and project management component under Loan 3715-GEO (F2) and Loan 3861-GEO (F4) will be harmonized for implementation: (i) road safety campaigns for both F2 and F4 will be done in May 2022 and 2023 during UN Road Safety week; (ii) project management training program will be planned by December 2021, the training arrangements finalized by August 2022, and delivered by end of 2022; and (iii) the road maintenance sustainability strategy draft - currently under MRDI's review - to be shared with ADB for review and comments.
Recruitment of Road Safety and Entrepreneurship and Livelihood Development Training consultants are ongoing. ADB approved the Submission 1 (CQS) for Road Safety and Entrepreneurship Consultant on 5 Jul and 11 Jul 2023, respectively.
ADB approved the Submission 2-3 (CQS) for Road Safety and Entrepreneurship Consultant on 16 October 2023.
Road Safety Awareness contract with Partnership for Road Safety Foundation signed on 1 November 2023. The contract was completed on 31 October 2024.
Entrepreneurship and Livelihood Development Training contract with Policy and Management Consulting Group (PMCG) signed on 31 October 2023. The contract was completed on 31 August 2024. Data Source: Road safety consultant's final report, approved by the Roads Department

Output: Road safety awareness increased Indicator: out of which at least 40% are women (2017 baseline: not applicable) Data Source: Road safety consultant's final report, approved by the Roads Department Actual value:

Output: Detailed design for E-60 Highway Section from Natakhtari to Rustavi (Tbilisi Bypass) Indicator: Detailed design, LARP, EIA, and bidding documents endorsed by ADB by December 2024 Progress/Status: Activity 1 (feasibility study) has been completed. The Consultant has submitted to Roads Department the inception and interim design reports for Activity 2 (detailed design).
A minor change in the project's scope was approved on 27 Sep 2019 to include preparation of detailed design for E-60 highway section from Natakhtari to Rustavi (Tbilisi Bypass) (as output iv). This scope was originally under L2843-GEO: Road Corridor Investment Program, Tranche 3 which closed on 29 September 2019.
On 23 Oct 2020, ADB approved Amendment No. 6 extending the contract until 15 Dec 2021 and amending the payment schedule and terms of reference.
The design reports for Lots 2 and 3 are expected to be submitted before end Nov 2021. The preparation of the EIA and LARP for Tbilisi Bypass is ongoing.
A consultation mission was fielded by ADB on 26-30 Jul 2021, and a wrap-up meeting was held on 10 Aug 2021 to discuss the ensuing loan. MOF noted that the timing of the project will depend on further internal consultations with MRDI/RD, and consequent deliberations of the fiscal space available in the coming years.
During the consultation mission fielded on 10-16 May 2022, the government confirmed that the candidate project Natakhtari-Jinvali will now be financed by state budget allocation.
On 27 Jul 2022, ADB approved the extension of the consultant's contract until 31 December 2022 (Amendment 9).
On 13 Jan 2023, ADB approved the extension of the consultant's contract until 30 June 2023 (Amendment 10).
During the Mar/Apr 2023 review mission, Roads Department indicated that extension of design consultant's contract until Dec 2023 (tentative target) is needed to complete the EIA for the 5 lots. Roads Department also requested the design consultant to split the EIA (prepare one for each lot, instead of one EIA) and to provide scoping reports for each lot.
ADB approved on 6 Jul 2023 the extension of the contract (Amendment 12) until 31 Dec 2023 with no cost implication.
The final design reports for Lot 1 (Natakhtari-Jinvali Section), Lot 2 (Tsitsamuri-Avchala), Lot 4 (Tbilisi Airport-Lochini Interchange), and Lot 5 (Lotchini Interchange-Rustavi) were submitted by RD in April 2023 and ADB has provided comments. Lot 3 (Avchala-Tbilisi Airport) is expected to be completed by November 2023. An extension of time is needed for environmental and social impact assessment.
ADB approved Amendment No. 13 on 9 Feb 2024 extending the contract of design consultant until 30 Jun 2024. The detailed designs of Lots, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 are ready. However, a time extension is required for the Consultant to obtain the environmental scoping conclusions and finalize the EIA reports for each lot.
ADB approved on 9 Feb 2024 the Amendment 13 which extends the design consultant's contract until 30 Jun 2024.
ADB approved on 2 Aug 2024 the Amendment 14 which extends the design consultant's contract until 31 Dec 2024.
ADB approved on 12 Feb 2025 the Amendment 15 to change the bank account details of design consultant.
Given that the loan is closed, RD approved Amendment 16 extending the contract completion date to 30 June 2025. The expenditures incurred under the contract will be financed by the government of Georgia.
